style: A calm, assured principal product engineer presenting to hackathon judges. Crisp international English, warm but restrained, consistently 130 to 140 words per minute, with only brief pauses around proof claims. Pronounce every letter separated by hyphens individually. Never sound theatrical or like an advertisement.

segments.text: Prediction apps ask whether Ether goes up or down. OutcomeGuard starts with exposure you already own, and turns a downside concern into bounded, verifiable protection.

Here, I define a $1,000 Ether exposure, a one-hour horizon, a 2-percent downside scenario, a 15 test U-S-D-C premium cap, 2-percent slippage, and 75-percent target protection. Structured controls remain authoritative; A-I never controls arithmetic or permissions.

Outcome Guard scopes the DreamDEX venue on Shannon chain number five, zero, three, one, two. It discovers an eligible Event Contract, verifies Trading on-chain, and reads the real book, spread, depth, expiry, settlement rule, and venue parameters.

The deterministic engine starts with portfolio loss, derives DOWN shares, then caps and quantizes by premium, executable depth, price impact, spread, lot size, and portfolio limits. The chart and receipt use this same calculation. Binary protection still carries basis risk.

Every control is visible. Required unknowns fail closed, and one policy engine runs at preview and before signing. Book movement, approaching expiry, or changed mandate inputs invalidate authorization.

This linked evidence is from Outcome Guard's Shannon test agent. A bounded I-O-C bought 4.171 shares of the NO outcome for 1.914489 test U-S-D-C. Confirmation requires the mined receipt, decoded fill, and reconciled position.

Intent, snapshot, hedge math, policy, authorization, and chain evidence use the S-H-A, two fifty six, digest algorithm. Any sealed change fails verification. Later lifecycle receipts link the previous digest rather than rewrite history.
The market resolved to the DOWN outcome. 4.171 test U-S-D-C became claimable, redemption succeeded, and the winning-token balance reached zero. Every stage remains independently inspectable.
OutcomeGuard makes Event Contracts a policy-bound protection layer for wallets and treasuries.
